claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for his A-levels. That's helpful.

Now I have a couple more questions to check your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and are you responsible for Alex (for example, does he live with you)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just one more question to complete the assessment:

**Are you already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?** Also, **is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him - this would be a new claim. And no, nobody else is claiming it for him either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me and the official eligibility criteria, I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me summarise your situation:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old
- Alex is in full-time approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you (so you are responsible for him)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- This would be a new claim

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex qualifies** because:
- Although he's 17 (over the standard age limit of 16), Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training
- A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved full-time non-advanced education
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**What to do next:**
You can make a new claim for Child Benefit. Please note that Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20. You'll need to inform the Child Benefit Office when Alex finishes his A-levels or if his circumstances change.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
